take_homes: Start from the teammate's job and what they use today, not from what I built. The thing I build competes with their current way of working.
Find the one obstacle that explains the others, and write the people plan with names, not blanks, next to the technical plan.
Ask what would have to be true for them to switch, then run one small test with one named person before building more.

monday.move: Sit down with the one pricing working group member who reads my pilot-cohort brief and ask how they use it today and what they do when it's late or wrong. Then write that into module-7/monday.md with the one assumption I'll test.
monday.who: The pricing working group member who consumes the pilot-cohort brief (finance side)
monday.when: Monday, in a 20-minute slot before the working group meeting
monday.stop_condition: If they say they never open the brief or already use something else, I stop building and rework the plan around that answer.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files. Everyone keeps their own copy, so even a good Monday result has nowhere to live.

misconception.why: I came in thinking better prompts were the skill. The module barely touched prompt quality. It was about the teammate's job, the people plan and whether they would switch. I don't fully let go of prompts, but they now look like the smaller part.

one_line: The core idea, interview for the job and test why they'd switch, is useful and I'm running it Monday, but cut the repeated filler paragraphs because they make the course look like it's padding.
